subtitle: Where Nine Cities Sleep Beneath One Name

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a stepped excavation pit under a blazing north Indian sun
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator stands on a wooden plank above a deep stepped trench, layers of exposed earth and ancient brick walls descending below him as the faint outline of a ruined stupa rises beyond the pit on the horizon.

dialogue.text: At Ahichhatra, where epic song, Jain memory and nine buried cities meet, each layer tells a different truth about Panchala’s forgotten capital.

i18n.hi: अहिच्छत्र, जहाँ महाकाव्य, जैन स्मृति और नौ दबे नगर मिलते हैं—हर तह पंचाल की भूली राजधानी की अलग सच्चाई कहती है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the Bareilly plain at dawn
panels.action: From high above, mist curls over the flat Ganga plain near Ramnagar; low mounds and scattered bricks break the fields as Ahichhatra Excavator, a survey notebook in hand, walks along a faint earthen rampart line with local villagers in the distance.

dialogue.text: On the Bareilly plain, near Ramnagar’s quiet fields, low mounds and broken bricks once puzzled surveyors. Was this the northern capital of ancient Panchala, long lost yet still named in epic lists?

i18n.hi: बरेली के मैदान पर, रामनगर के शांत खेतों के पास, छोटे टीले और टूटी ईंटें कभी नापतौल वालों को चकित करती थीं—क्या ये प्राचीन पंचाल की उत्तर राजधानी थी, जो खो गई पर सूचियों में अब भी दर्ज है?

panels.shot: mid-shot of Excavator kneeling by a brick fragment, horizon low to show surrounding mounds
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator crouches, turning a weathered brick in his hands near a shallow trench; behind him rise several broad rounded mounds, hinting at buried bastions and a city wall.

dialogue.speaker: Ahichhatra Excavator
dialogue.text: A rampart, a moat line… and a name in old lists. Could this be Ahichhatra?

i18n.hi: किले-दीवार, खाई की लकीर… और पुरानी सूचियों में एक नाम। क्या यही अहिच्छत्र है?

panels.shot: slow push-in on an old survey map and palm-leaf style text laid out together
panels.action: On a wooden table, Ahichhatra Excavator’s hands spread an ASI survey map beside a copied page of a Puranic-style geographical list; faint lines mark Panchala’s rivers and a dot labelled in English as ‘Ahichhatra’ near Ramnagar.

dialogue.text: Textual geography spoke of a northern Panchala capital, somewhere between the Ganga and the Himalaya’s edge. Cunningham’s surveys matched those lines to these mounds, but names alone could not prove a city’s past.

i18n.hi: पुस्तकों में उत्तर पंचाल की राजधानी गंगा और हिमालय की तराई के बीच कहीं बताई गई थी। कनिंघम की नापें इन टीलों से मिल गईं, पर सिर्फ नाम से शहर का अतीत साबित नहीं होता।

panels.shot: wide shot of early 20th century camp at the mound edge
panels.action: Tents, measuring rods, and a hand-pulled cart of tools cluster at the foot of a large mound as Ahichhatra Excavator directs labourers placing pegs to mark a rectangular trench under the hazy afternoon light.

dialogue.text: In the 1940s, K.K. Sinha and his team cut deep into the mound. Spades, baskets and careful notes would test the belief that this was Panchala’s seat, and reveal how many cities had risen here.

i18n.hi: 1940 के दशक में के.के. सिन्हा और उनकी टीम ने टीले में गहरी कटानें लगाईं। फावड़े, टोकरियाँ और बारीक नोट यह परखने उतरे कि क्या सचमुच यही पंचाल की गद्दी थी, और यहाँ कितने नगर उगे।

panels.shot: vertical cross-sectional view, camera aligned with a deep trench wall
panels.action: Looking along a high trench face, distinct horizontal bands of soil and brickwork step downwards; Ahichhatra Excavator points with his staff at alternating layers of compact mud, burnt brick lines and ash, while workers stand on different ledges.

dialogue.text: Layer after layer emerged. Sinha counted nine main occupation levels, from pre-Mauryan depths through Kushan and Gupta splendour into early medieval shrines, each city built atop the ruins of another.

i18n.hi: एक पर एक परत उठती गई। सिन्हा ने नौ बड़े बसावट-स्तर गिने—मौर्य-पूर्व गहराइयों से लेकर कुषाण-गुप्त वैभव और प्राचीन मंदिरों तक—हर नया नगर पिछले के खंडहरों पर सजा।

panels.shot: close-up on trowel scraping an early brick alignment
panels.action: A trowel in Ahichhatra Excavator’s hand carefully clears soil from a rough, thick brick wall deep in the trench, the texture of the bricks coarse and uneven compared to later courses above.

dialogue.text: The lowest levels showed crude brick and mud fortifications, earlier than the Mauryan age. They hinted at a fortified settlement in the time of the mahajanapadas, yet gave no clear king’s name, no royal seal of Panchala.

i18n.hi: सबसे नीचे की परतों में कच्ची ईंट और मिट्टी की किलेबंदी मिली, मौर्यों से भी पुरानी। ये महाजनपदों के समय के एक दुर्ग-नगर की ओर इशारा करती हैं, पर न कोई राजा का नाम, न पंचाल की शाही मुहर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Excavator examining potsherds and early terracottas on a tray
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator stands under a canvas awning, studying a tray of grey ware sherds and simple terracotta figurines laid out in neat rows, while an assistant labels them with small tags.

dialogue.text: Grey wares and early terracottas matched the broad horizon of sixth century BCE north India. They showed life in a time when Panchala, Kuru and Kosala contended, but they did not shout, ‘This is Drupada’s court.’

i18n.hi: धूसर मृद्भांड और शुरुआती मिट्टी की मूर्तियाँ छठी सदी ईसा पूर्व के उत्तर भारत से मेल खाती हैं। ये वो दौर दिखाती हैं जब पंचाल, कुरु और कौशल टकराते थे, पर ये नहीं चिल्लातीं—‘यहाँ द्रुपद का दरबार था!’

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Excavator holding a later stone ayagapata just raised from a trench
panels.action: From a mid-level trench, workers haul up a rectangular stone ayagapata on a rope; Ahichhatra Excavator leans in, eyes intent, as the panel’s carved railing motifs and seated figures catch the light.

dialogue.text: Higher up, stone spoke more clearly. Jain ayagapatas from the early centuries CE bore railings, shrines and names of donors. Ahichhatra had become a sacred site, a place where lay Jains earned merit through gifts of stone.

i18n.hi: ऊपर की परतों में पत्थर ज्यादा साफ बोलते हैं। आरंभिक शताब्दियों के जैन आयागपटों पर रेलिंग, मंदिर और दाताओं के नाम उकेरे हैं। अहिच्छत्र एक पवित्र जैन स्थल बन चुका था, जहाँ गृहस्थ पत्थर-दान से पुण्य कमाते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on inscription band of an ayagapata as Excavator traces letters
panels.action: In a study hut, Ahichhatra Excavator bends over the ayagapata, finger gently tracing a line of early Brahmi letters on its edge while a magnifying glass and ink copy rest nearby.

dialogue.text: Inscribed names, catalogued later in Lüders’ lists, fixed some stones to the early centuries of our era. Yet even these Jain records, clear and pious, did not speak of mahajanapada politics two hundred years before Ashoka.

i18n.hi: इन नामों को बाद में ल्यूडर्स की सूचियों ने हमारी आरंभिक शताब्दियों में ठिकाने लगाया। पर ये साफ, भक्तिमय जैन अभिलेख भी अशोक से दो सौ साल पहले की महाजनपद राजनीति पर खामोश हैं।

panels.shot: mid-shot with Excavator facing a colleague, holding a labelled stratigraphy drawing
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator stands beside a pinned stratigraphic section drawing, its nine layers inked and annotated; he gestures from lower to upper levels as a colleague listens thoughtfully in the lamplight.

dialogue.speaker: Ahichhatra Excavator
dialogue.text: This Nandighosha ayagapata belongs up here, centuries later. It cannot prove a sixth-century capital.

i18n.hi: यह नंदिघोष आयागपट यहीं ऊपर की परतों का है, सदियों बाद का। यह छठी सदी की राजधानी साबित नहीं कर सकता।

panels.shot: wider shot showing a partially exposed stupa and temple foundations on the mound top
panels.action: On the mound’s crest, Ahichhatra Excavator walks past the circular brick drum of a stupa and rectangular foundations of a later shrine, open to the sky and ringed by piles of carved fragments.

dialogue.text: Quintanilla later traced Ahichhatra’s sculptures to a vibrant Kushan and Gupta era centre, tied to Mathura’s stone workshops. The city’s religious life thickened as political memories faded, leaving shrines where ramparts once ruled.

i18n.hi: क्विन्तानिला ने बाद में अहिच्छत्र की मूर्तियों को एक जीवंत कुषाण-गुप्त केंद्र से जोड़ा, जो मथुरा की पत्थर कार्यशालाओं से बँधा था। शहर का धार्मिक जीवन गहराता गया, पर पुरानी सत्ता-दीवारों की याद धुंधली होकर मंदिरों में ढल गई।

panels.shot: close-up on a broken sculpted panel showing Jain imagery resting beside a cracked brick
panels.action: A broken sculpted panel with a Jain motif lies propped against a crumbling brick from an older wall; Ahichhatra Excavator’s hand hovers between them, as if weighing one against the other.

dialogue.text: Archaeology showed a city that outlived the mahajanapadas, becoming a Jain tirtha and later sacred mound. But the lowest layers, poorly published and silent in inscription, still left the earliest Ahichhatra half in shadow.

i18n.hi: खुदाई ने दिखाया कि यह नगर महाजनपदों के बाद भी जिया—पहले जैन तीर्थ, फिर पवित्र टीला बना। पर सबसे निचली, अधूरे ढंग से छपी और शिलालेख-विहीन परतें आरंभिक अहिच्छत्र को आधा अँधेरा ही छोड़ती हैं।

panels.shot: intercut-style shot: Excavator in camp, with a ghosted backdrop of Mahabharata court scene
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator sits by his lantern writing, while behind him, faintly suggested like a memory, a painterly vision shows a Mahabharata-era court with a teacher and king facing each other in tension.

dialogue.text: The Mahabharata’s tale of Drona and Drupada had fixed Ahichhatra in epic imagination as Panchala’s proud seat. Yet Sinha’s trenches reminded scholars that epic fame is not a dated inscription, and story is not stratigraphy.

i18n.hi: महाभारत की द्रोण-द्रुपद कथा ने अहिच्छत्र को कल्पना में पंचाल की गौरव-राजधानी बना दिया था। पर सिन्हा की खाइयों ने विद्वानों को याद दिलाया कि महाकाव्य की शोहरत तारीख लगा हुआ अभिलेख नहीं होती, और कहानी परत-दर-परत खुदाई नहीं है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Excavator addressing a small gathering of students on the mound
panels.action: Under a tree beside the mound, Ahichhatra Excavator explains with animated hands to a circle of students, using a simple sketch of the nine layers drawn in the dust before them.

dialogue.speaker: Ahichhatra Excavator
dialogue.text: We honour the epic, but we must let each layer keep its own date.

i18n.hi: हम महाकाव्य का मान रखते हैं, पर हर परत को उसकी अपनी तारीख पर रहने देना होगा।

panels.shot: evening wide shot of the mound and trenches bathed in sunset light
panels.action: As the sun sets, long shadows fill the trenches; Ahichhatra Excavator stands alone on the mound edge, overlooking the stepped cuts and the faint outline of ancient walls now glowing softly in the orange light.

dialogue.text: By the time the trenches fell silent, Ahichhatra was no longer just a name from lists. It had become a layered record of Panchala’s rise and afterlife, from ramparts to relics.

i18n.hi: जब तक खाइयों में फावड़े थमे, अहिच्छत्र सिर्फ सूचियों का नाम नहीं रहा। यह पंचाल के उत्थान और उसके बाद के जीवन की परतदार कहानी बन चुका था—किले-दीवारों से लेकर अवशेषों तक।

panels.shot: close-up on Excavator closing his field diary, camera over his shoulder to show the words "Nine strata"
panels.action: Ahichhatra Excavator gently closes a worn field diary, its open page briefly showing neat lines summarizing the nine occupation strata before the cover meets with a soft thud.

dialogue.text: Today, Ahichhatra teaches how cities can be remembered one way in song, another in Jain stone, and yet another in earth—reminding us that the past is clearest when every layer, and every voice, keeps its date.

i18n.hi: आज अहिच्छत्र सिखाता है कि नगर गीतों में एक तरह से याद होते हैं, जैन पत्थरों में दूसरी तरह से, और धरती की परतों में तीसरी तरह से—याद दिलाते हुए कि अतीत तभी सबसे साफ दिखता है, जब हर परत और हर आवाज अपनी तारीख पर टिकी रहे।
